## Key Simplification of $S_1$

$S_1(n) - S_1(n-1) = \sum_{i: i^2|n} \mathbf{1}[n/i^2 \text{ square-free}]$. For $n = \prod p_i^{a_i}$, the valid $i = \prod p_i^{b_i}$ requires $b_i \leq \lfloor a_i/2\rfloor$ and $a_i - 2b_i \leq 1$. $$\Delta S_2(n) = S_2(n)-S_2(n-1) = \sum_{m|n,\; n/m\text{ sf}} d(m) = \sum_{k|\text{rad}(n)} d(n/k)$$

Writing $n = \prod p_i^{a_i}$, each prime factor independently contributes $\sum_{s\in\{0,1\}}(a_i - s + 1) = (a_i+1)+a_i = 2a_i+1$, so:

$$\boxed{\Delta S_2(n) = \prod_{p^a \| n} (2a+1) =: g(n)}$$
